newsitem.title: EGYPT: Israeli defence minister sees Egyptian president.
newsitem.headline: Israeli defence minister sees Egyptian president.

text.p: Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai met Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak in the Egyptian Red Sea resort of Hurghada on Tuesday in an attempt to save relations between Israel and Egypt.

"I very much hope that we will succeed today in finding additional ways... to strengthen peace with the Egyptians and to seek understanding between the Israeli government and the Egyptian government," the Israeli minister told reporters en route to Egypt.
"That can be an important contribution to the overall regional security," he added.

Mordechai and Mubarak will also discuss the latest developments in Israeli-Palestinian negotiations on the West Bank town of Hebron, which seemed on Tuesday to be moving closer to an agreement, officials said.

Israeli officials have criticised Egypt's pro-Palestinian role in the negotiations which they say is complicating matters but Egyptian radio said Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had telephoned Mubarak late on Monday to brief him on progress in the talks.
"Egypt plays an important role in the advancement of the peace process since it was the first Arab state to sign a peace agreement with Israel," Mordechai said in a statement on Monday.
It is Mordechai's first visit to Egypt since he and his rightwing Likud party were elected in May.
Egypt, which made peace with Israel in 1979, has been a vociferous critic of Likud policies, especially its drive to expand settlements in the West Bank.
Visits to Egypt by Israeli ministers have become much less frequent than under the previous Labour Party government.
